To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The O2 A- (757–774nm) and B- (684–688nm) bands are useful for the retrieval of particulate optical depth and vertical profile of particulates over dark surfaces.

(1) SCIAMACHY O2 A- & B-bands provide additional information on the particulate matter vertical profile, (2) our retrieval is applicable to both bright and dark surfaces and (3) it can provide a stable estimate of the particulate matter optical thickness.

we have demonstrated the retrieval of particulate optical thickness, particle size, and the vertical profile of the particulate matter from SCIAMACHY O2 A- (757–774) and B-band (684-688) measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a retrieval algorithm for the retrieval of the vertical distribution of particulates from space.
the feasibility of using SCIAMACHY to provide global information about the vertical profile of atmospheric aerosol and cloud particles, and to provide a basis for the design of future instruments.
the retrieval of particulate optical thickness and vertical distribution of scatterers using SCIAMACHY O 2 A-band and B-band observations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the O2 A and B bands are useful for the retrieval of the aerosol optical depth and the vertical distribution of particulates in the atmosphere, and that the combined use of these two bands is advantageous over the use of either one of them individually.

the O2 B- and A-bands are useful for the retrieval of particulate microphysical parameters in addition to their optical thickness, but the information content of the O2 A-band alone is insufficient for such a purpose.
the retrieval of the vertical distribution of aerosol/cloud using the O2 A-band is feasible, and that it is enhanced by the use of part of the O 2 B-band.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and demonstrated the feasibility of a physics-based algorithm to retrieve particulate optical thickness and vertical distribution of atmospheric aerosols and clouds from SCIAMACHY measurements, which is a first of its kind.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of retrieving aerosol/cloud vertical distributions using O2 A- & B-band observations, which is a step forward towards a global aerosol/cloud climatology.
we have demonstrated the potential of using the O2 B- and A-bands in combination to retrieve the vertical profile of aerosol/cloud, in addition to the particulate optical thickness, using SCIAMACHY.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combined use of the A-band with a small part of the B-band is sufficient to retrieve the vertical distribution of particulates, and that the B-band is an additional source of information on aerosol vertical distribution, in addition to the well-known O2 A-band.

the combined use of the O2 A-band and part of the B-band in a physics-based retrieval of aerosols can provide valuable information on the vertical profile of atmospheric particulates, which is currently missing in most aerosol remote sensing algorithms, and is a step forward towards the goal of a global monitoring of the aerosol vertical distribution from space.
a combined use of O2 A- (or B-) band and O2 B- (or A-) band can provide additional information about the vertical distribution of particulates.
